issue.title: sase-core just check omits the selected Python shared-library path
issue.description: Discovered by sase-xq.land.r0--1 while landing sase-xq. Core scripts/check.sh selects a qualifying interpreter but does not arrange its runtime library directory, so uv-managed Python can compile the PyO3 tests yet fail to start them. Monitor 49vf71b1wanp failed on core 93fe02b with libpython3.14.so.1.0 missing from loader paths. The library exists, and prepending that interpreter sysconfig LIBDIR makes the same binary list all 116 binding tests. The main SASE rust-test recipe already provides this environment. Fix the core verification launcher to derive the needed loader path from its selected interpreter while preserving overrides and existing paths; verify full core just check with a uv-managed Linux interpreter. Small scope because the exact launcher omission and successful loader repair are proven. Source dates to 865da85, before sase-xq. Duplicate searches across all task statuses/types and the last-week sweep found no task; sase-xs only records owners using temporary environment workarounds. The 27 active epic scopes contain no causal owner. No source repair is being launched by this report.

task_type_fields.impact: Blocks the required whole-workspace core verification, including PyO3 binding tests, until each caller supplies an undocumented runtime-library workaround.
task_type_fields.repro: Run core just check with uv-managed Python 3.14 selected and no interpreter LIBDIR in LD_LIBRARY_PATH; cargo test --workspace reaches sase_core_rs then exits 127 loading libpython3.14.so.1.0. Set LD_LIBRARY_PATH from the chosen interpreter sysconfig LIBDIR and the same test binary --list starts successfully.

payload.description: Adjacent sase-core just check lane defect discovered by an agent running the repository-wide core check; fixes touch the same core verification entry point

evidence.note: Independent reproduction from proposing phase sase-yh.5.1 during land audit: on sase-core v0.32.54 (e2836d8), plain ./scripts/check.sh test selected uv Python 3.14, completed the Rust suites, then the sase_core_rs PyO3 test binary exited 127 because libpython3.14.so.1.0 was absent from the loader path. This confirms the existing task's exact scripts/check.sh root cause and blocks an unassisted full core verification.

PROPOSED BY phase sase-yw.3.1 note #1; independently reproduced by sase-yw.3 landing monitor ctqf1ce930m4 on core 7444d15 (v0.32.61). Plain just check selected uv Python 3.14, passed ordinary Rust suites, then sase_core_rs exited 127 because libpython3.14.so.1.0 was absent from the loader path (SASE_YW3_CORE_CHECK_STATUS=127). This is the exact scripts/check.sh root cause already tracked here; no new task created.

Independent reproduction while working sase-xe.16.11.7.14.3 on 2026-09-10: plain ./scripts/check.sh and PYO3_PYTHON=/home/bryan/.local/bin/python3.12 ./scripts/check.sh both completed Rust suites then failed at the sase_core_rs PyO3 test binary with exit 127 loading libpython3.14.so.1.0 / libpython3.12.so.1.0. Rerunning the same gate with PYO3_PYTHON=/home/bryan/.local/bin/python3.12 and LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/home/bryan/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.12.13-linux-x86_64-gnu/lib passed.

LAND AUDIT of sase-xe.16.11.7.14: proposal from phase sase-xe.16.11.7.14.1 note #1 is the same loader omission. Independently inspected core e0f105d scripts/check.sh: resolve_pyo3_python exports PYO3_PYTHON, cmd_test immediately invokes cargo test --workspace, and the file never arranges LD_LIBRARY_PATH. This still requires a caller workaround for the fleet repair verification. Phase .3 already supplied this epic's runtime reproduction on 2026-09-10; this report adds source/impact evidence, not a claimed new runtime reproduction. No duplicate task created. Audit artifact: file:explicit:e2c64521530457f9913aa9aa.

Independent reproduction while working sase-zq.1 on 2026-09-11: ./scripts/check.sh all selected uv Python 3.14, completed sase_core unit tests (2567 passed), then the sase_core_rs PyO3 test binary exited 127 loading libpython3.14.so.1.0. Rerun with LD_LIBRARY_PATH set to that interpreter sysconfig LIBDIR passed the full workspace tests including bead_action_bindings_round_trip_json_shapes.

PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP disposition for sase-zt.1 note #1: phase observed default core just check selecting python3.14 then failing to load libpython3.14.so.1.0, while PYO3_PYTHON=/usr/bin/python3 passed. Land audit independently inspected current core scripts/check.sh: resolve_pyo3_python checks only interpreter version and cmd_test immediately runs cargo test --workspace without adding the selected LIBDIR to the loader path. Same proven root cause as this task; preserve explicit interpreter/loader workaround for verification. No fresh Rust runtime failure claimed and no duplicate task.
